section: 7-Eleven Store Support Center: auditorium, video walls, displays and conferencing equipment in the AVI-SPL project
body:
This part of the 7-Eleven case study describes the auditorium and the campus-wide AV equipment at the Store Support Center. It is legacy-platform proof: video ran on Polycom and the Skype for Business infrastructure, the older platforms named on the page.

**The auditorium**

- A 6,000-square foot room that divides three ways. It is used every day for work such as live sound mixing and video and web conferencing.
- Every two weeks it hosts the all-hands events, which go out as a broadcast to the satellite sites of 7-Eleven.
- Vaddio cameras, mounted on the ceiling and walls, feed the Polycom video system and the Skype for Business infrastructure.
- Wide audio coverage comes from about 30 wireless mics by ClearOne in several styles (handheld, gooseneck, ceiling) and from dozens of Polycom microphones.
- JT Elliott of 7-Eleven said meetings and requests change all the time and the room has to be flexible; the ClearOne wireless system lets staff put microphones wherever they want around the room.

**Displays, projectors and video walls**

- 7-Eleven uses NEC in its stores, so NEC integration was supported across the campus, including the auditorium. AV staff use controls such as RS-232, CEC and LAN to monitor and control those displays through the Crestron Fusion platform.
- The Epson projectors also offer Crestron connectivity. Their high-lumen output is described as a major benefit in the large meeting rooms and the auditorium.
- There are three Planar video walls. One, in the auditorium, is a bezel-free LED wall; another is in the lobby. The lobby wall promotes 7-Eleven and is sometimes used to greet vendors and guests with personalized messages, which Elliott said shows them they are valued.

**Video conferencing and audio processing**

- Polycom drives the video conferencing in the Store Support Center and across 30-plus corporate sites, through a combination of bridges and cloud licenses.
- Polycom digital signal processors handle the audio from ceiling mics in the large integrated audio rooms and in the auditorium.

**Working relationship**

- Elliott said what impressed him most was the first conversation with the AVI-SPL sales team: they understood the vision and were not afraid to say what would not work and what they liked.
- During the project an unexpected problem appeared with a few CAT-5 modular plugs. Elliott said AVI-SPL returned to the rooms already installed and replaced every one of them, which showed 7-Eleven that AVI-SPL was on its side.

**When to use this**

For questions about proof of a divisible auditorium, all-hands broadcast spaces, video walls or display control in a corporate campus project.
